question: What is the name of the autobiography written by the 14th Dalai Lama?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Freedom in Exile**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Freedom in Exile** is the autobiography of the 14th Dalai Lama, Tenzin Gyatso.
 
• The book was first published in **1990**.
 
• It provides a detailed account of the Dalai Lama’s early life, his escape from Tibet, and his life in exile.
 
• The autobiography highlights the Tibetan struggle for freedom and the Dalai Lama's efforts to preserve Tibetan culture and identity.
 
• The book is widely regarded as an important work for understanding the life and philosophy of the Dalai Lama.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **14th Dalai Lama**

 
 
• Born on July 6, 1935, as Lhamo Thondup in Taktser, Amdo, Tibet.
 
• Recognized as the reincarnation of the 13th Dalai Lama at the age of two.
 
• Enthroned as the spiritual leader of Tibet in 1940.
 
• Fled to India in 1959 following the Tibetan uprising against Chinese rule.
 
• Awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1989 for his non-violent struggle for the liberation of Tibet.
 
 
 
• **Tibetan Buddhism**
 
 
• A form of Mahayana Buddhism that evolved in Tibet and the Himalayan region.
 
• Combines the essential teachings of Mahayana Buddhism with Tantric and Shamanic elements.
 
• The Dalai Lama is considered the spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism.
 
• Focuses on the path to enlightenment through meditation, moral conduct, and wisdom.
 
 
 
• **Tibetan Government in Exile**
 
 
• Also known as the Central Tibetan Administration (CTA).
 
• Established in 1959 after the Dalai Lama and thousands of Tibetans fled to India.
 
• Based in Dharamshala, India.
 
• Works to preserve Tibetan culture, promote human rights, and seek a peaceful resolution to the Tibet issue.
 
 
 
• **Non-violence and Compassion**
 
 
• Core principles advocated by the Dalai Lama.
 
• Emphasizes the importance of compassion, kindness, and forgiveness.
 
• Promotes peaceful resolution of conflicts and respect for all forms of life.
 
• Inspired by the teachings of Buddha and Mahatma Gandhi.
